cross-013.answer: Skiff runs Tern at the Performance preset, saving 1.8 ms over Quality (3.9 ms vs 2.1 ms), per dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3.

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. The co-op rollback netcode prototype was abandoned: dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b stopped it because re-running tide simulation on every rollback frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff. The shader compile cache and build farm was completed once the cache ran on every farm build (dec-turn-the-shader-compile-cache-on-for-every-farm--4rr3b12b4sasdmaj), as its retrospective fnd-retrospective-on-the-shader-compile-cache--9rpv2a60ach04cx6 records, with clean rebuilds down from 47 minutes to 6 min 40 s.

netcode-004.answer: The team dropped rollback because each rollback frame must re-run the tide simulation, costing 4.8 ms of a 25 ms frame on Skiff, and quarter-resolution re-simulation desynced within 90 seconds. The reason depends on the world Decision dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e, which keeps tides deterministic and which co-op needs.

ports-012.answer: The team raised the floor to 576p because caustic patterns under saltglass shimmered badly at the 540p floor even with Tern (dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb, derived from fnd-saltglass-caustics-shimmer-at-the-540p-floor--0aa8sts89vhq1s6q).

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: The third version, dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9, moved foliage and saltglass out of the buffer to render them in a forward pass after the resolve: alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the buffer versus 0.8 ms in forward, and saltglass refracts the resolved scene, so it needs that scene to exist first.

render-032.answer: Tern was chosen as Lantern's only upscaler (decision dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e): Halcyon has no Skiff build, and shipping two upscalers would break the one-upscaler constraint. Owning the code also mattered more than raw quality for saltglass, since the team can change Tern upscaling the same week without a vendor ticket or license.

render-046.answer: Reopened on 2026-01-12 because the 3.1 ms cost finding that rejected it was a capture error; with cached pages, virtual shadow maps cost 1.4 ms, less than four cascades (dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4).

render-047.answer: Because the release-build capture put the visibility buffer on Skiff at 7.4 ms against 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), so keeping the forward+ fallback was no longer worth it, and maintaining two opaque paths cost about one engineer-week a month. Record: dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1

world-036.answer: Kestrel retired the fiber scheduler for engine jobs on 2026-04-14 (record dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h) because 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack, which blocked crash triage for beta, and a continuation-based thread pool kept workers 93% busy, close to the 95% fibers gave.

world-051.answer: Because integer adds and multiplies in 32.32 fixed point give identical bits on every CPU and compiler, while float tides drifted apart between machines within 6 minutes; the strict IEEE float decision was rejected in favor of this (dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e).

world-055.answer: Kelp stays because the cold-cache rerun that favored Zstandard tested the 4 MB dictionary; shrinking Kelp's dictionary to 1 MB makes it beat Zstandard cold on Skiff by 1.7x, per dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew.
